The Newton’s law of cooling holds true in the following conditions: a) The difference in temperature between the body and the surroundings must be small.
b) The loss of heat from the body should only be caused by radiation.
c) Temperature of the surroundings must remain constant during the cooling.

11.8 Principle of Calorimetry Can you answer this?

A student claims that when two bodies at different temperatures are brought in thermal contact, fall in temperature of hotter body must be equal to the rise in temperature of the colder one. Is it acceptable?

When two objects at different temperatures are brought into thermal contact, the hot ter object loses the heat while the colder object gains the heat until both reach to an equal temperature. If heat loss to the surroundings is prevented, the quantity of heat lost by the hot ter body is equal to the quantity of heat gained by the colder body. This is the principle of calorimetry. It can be stated that the amount of the heat lost by a hotter body must be equal to amount of the heat gained by a colder body during the process of heat exchange between two objects in a closed system.

That is, heat loss= heat gain ; for a closed system. A closed system is also called an isolated system. In a closed system objects under consideration do not exchange heat with its surroundings. Principle of calorimetry is an alternative form of the law of conservation of energy. Idea of principle of calorimetry is used to calculate specific heat capacity of different substances.
